# Checkpoint 5: UI done and committed

**Commit `458e868f`** (4 files). The branch now has three commits on top of master: `78523efe` (state), `027e95ef` (enforcement), `458e868f` (UI). Nothing is pushed.

**Results:** all 9 lock and visibility suites pass (**Test Files 9 passed (9) · Tests 247 passed | 30 skipped**); typecheck, ESLint and prettier are clean. The final full-suite run comes at Checkpoint 6.

## What the dropdown has now

- **A lock toggle on every row** (in the room, previously seen, and Untagged & unknown), right of the eye.
  - Visible collaborator: the toggle works normally.
  - Hidden collaborator: disabled and shown locked (C). The tooltip says why.
  - Your own row: disabled and shown unlocked (H).
- **"Lock all" / "Unlock all"** on a second row of buttons under Show all / Hide all. Unlock all is greyed out while no _visible_ collaborator is locked.
- **Desktop and mobile:** it's the same component in both places, so the phone main menu gets everything too. The phone layout has its own test.
- **#116's tests:** unchanged and passing. The eye button keeps its test id, `aria-pressed` and text; it now sits in a wrapper next to the lock button.
- **12 component tests:** 11 on desktop, 1 on the phone layout. They cover A, B, C, H and the miscellaneous row.

## Manual verification (two browsers)

Setup: the room server (`cd excalidraw-room && yarn start:dev`), the app (`yarn start`), then **Browser A** (you) and **Browser B** (incognito, "Bob") in the same room. Draw a rectangle and a short text in **B**, and a rectangle in **A**.

1. **A:** open **⋯** → every row has 👁 plus 🔓. Your own 🔓 is greyed out.
2. **A:** lock Bob → his drawings **stay visible** and his icon turns 🔒.
3. **A:** test each blocked interaction:
   - click Bob's rectangle → nothing is selected
   - drag it → a selection box appears instead and nothing moves
   - drag a box over both rectangles → only yours is selected
   - Ctrl+A → only yours
   - Delete → only yours disappears (Ctrl+Z to bring it back)
   - eraser across Bob's rectangle → it survives
   - double-click Bob's text → it doesn't open for editing (a new empty text box opens instead; press Esc)
   - double-click Bob's rectangle → no label is added to it
4. **A:** draw an arrow from your rectangle to Bob's → it **binds**, and Bob's rectangle doesn't move (amended E).
5. **B:** nothing changed when A locked or unlocked. B moves Bob's rectangle → A sees it move (F).
6. **A:** hide Bob (👁) → his 🔒 is shown locked and greyed out. Show him again → still 🔒. Click it → 🔓, and his shapes are selectable again (C).
7. **A:** Lock all → everyone except you is 🔒. Hide Bob, then Unlock all → the others unlock, but Bob stays 🔒 (B).
8. **A:** reload the page → everyone is unlocked again (G).
9. **Mobile:** in DevTools turn on the device toolbar and pick a phone → ☰ → Collaborators → **⋯** → the same controls work.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-12 00:30:16Z)**_

Confirmed. This is a gap in my Checkpoint 5 UI, and it comes from the same blind spot you describe: I worked out Unlock all's enabled state from the lock list, but never gave Lock all one at all. The right rule follows from "no interactivity without visibility": **a bulk button is enabled only if at least one listed collaborator would actually change.**

| Button | Enabled when | After Hide all |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lock all | someone **visible**, other than me, is **unlocked** | disabled: nobody is visible |
| Unlock all | someone **visible**, other than me, is **locked** | disabled: hidden people stay locked |

Both checks will use the dropdown's own rows (`isLocked`, `isLockDisabled`), so the buttons always agree with what the toggles show. The check goes in one pure function in [visibility.ts](packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts), so StrykerJS can mutation-test it directly.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-12 00:32:10Z)**_

I've fixed the bug. **Lock all** is now greyed out after **Hide all**; Unlock all was already greyed out there. Committed as its own fix commit, `09013e13`, on top of the Checkpoint 5 commit.

**The cause:** Lock all never had a rule for when it should be disabled, so it stayed clickable even when it could do nothing. Unlock all had a rule, but it read the lock list directly instead of what the dropdown shows.

**The fix:** both buttons now follow one rule from the dropdown's own rows. A button is only clickable if at least one row it would change exists: a visible collaborator other than you. Hidden collaborators (always locked) and your own row (never locked) don't count.

| Situation | Lock all | Unlock all |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh room | ✅ | greyed out |
| Everyone visible is locked | greyed out | ✅ |
| **After Hide all** | **greyed out** | **greyed out** |
| Hide all → Show all (everyone stays locked, per C) | greyed out | ✅ |
| One hidden, another visible and unlocked | ✅ | greyed out |

**Tests:** I wrote the new UI tests before the fix. Three of them failed on the old code, each with "Lock all should be greyed out but isn't", which is exactly what you saw. After the fix:

- all 9 suites pass: 259 passed, 30 skipped (the same `frame.test.tsx` skips as on master)
- typecheck and ESLint are clean

There are 12 new tests: 6 click the buttons in the dropdown, and 6 call the new rule function directly.

**Where it changed:**

- The rule: `getBulkLockAvailability` at [visibility.ts:217](packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts#L217). It's pure, so StrykerJS can mutate it.
- The dropdown uses it at [CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx:185](packages/excalidraw/components/CollaboratorVisibility/CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx#L185), and the two buttons' greyed-out state at lines 222 and 233. This replaces the old Unlock all check.

**To re-check by hand:** click Hide all; both Lock all and Unlock all should be greyed out. Click Show all; only Unlock all should be clickable.

Waiting for "continue" to start Checkpoint 6, the final checks and the `pr-81.md` draft.

Closes #81 (Sub-issue)

## What changed

Adds a local, per-collaborator **lock** (visible-only mode) to the collaborator dropdown. A locked collaborator's drawings stay visible on my screen, but I can't select, move, resize, rotate, delete, erase, or text-edit them. Everything is local to my client: nothing is synced, saved, or exported, and other collaborators notice nothing.

This is a **carryover of #80 via #116**: #80 asked for per-collaborator visibility _and_ interactivity controls. #116 delivered visibility (ownership via `customData.creatorId`, the central rule in `element/ownership.ts`, the dropdown). This PR delivers the interactivity half, built on the same structures.

### The rule (one pure function)

- `isCollaboratorInteractive` in `packages/element/src/ownership.ts`: **hidden → never interactive** (no interactivity without visibility); **your own bucket → always interactive** (can't be locked); otherwise **locked → not interactive**.
- Pure lock-list helpers next to it: `addLockedCollaborators`, `toggleLockedCollaborator` (ignored while hidden or for yourself), `unlockVisibleCollaborators` (hidden collaborators stay locked).
- Element-level wrappers `isElementInteractive` / `excludeNonInteractiveElements` (bound text follows its container; never-seen creators and untagged elements follow the miscellaneous bucket, as in #116).

### State and actions

- `AppState.lockedCollaboratorIds` (default empty; `browser`/`export`/`server` all `false`, so it's never persisted, exported, or synced and resets on reload).
- New actions `toggleCollaboratorLock`, `lockAllCollaborators`, `unlockAllCollaborators`. All use `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` (no history, nothing to sync).
- #116's hide actions (per-collaborator toggle and "Hide all") now also lock whoever they hide, so a collaborator who is shown again stays locked until unlocked (Criteria C).

### Enforcement

Interaction chokepoints now ask the interactivity rule instead of the visibility-only check: hit testing (click select, double-click text edit, path-target pick), `selectGroupsForSelectedElements` (marquee, lasso, Select All, groups), the App selection safety net (also re-run when the lock list changes), and the eraser. Rendering, export, search, and **arrow binding** stay visibility-only: per the amended Criteria E, arrows may still bind to locked (visible) elements, never to hidden ones. The element's built-in `locked` property is not used (it syncs and would break Criteria F).

### UI

Each dropdown row (in the room, previously seen, and "Untagged & unknown") gets a lock toggle beside its visibility toggle: disabled and shown locked while the collaborator is hidden, disabled and shown unlocked on your own row. "Lock all" / "Unlock all" are enabled only when they'd change something (both disabled after "Hide all"). Same component on desktop and in the phone main menu. #116's row button is unchanged (same test id, `aria-pressed`, text), now wrapped next to the lock button.

### Commits

- `78523efe` state logic · `027e95ef` enforcement · `458e868f` UI · `09013e13` fix: bulk buttons disabled when they'd change nothing (found in manual testing) · `d7e29804` repair mis-encoded characters in test names

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- Tests look actions up by name (`h.app.actionManager.actions[name]`) so a missing action fails as a readable assertion; a renamed action is only caught at test time, not by the type checker.
- `getSelectionWithoutHiddenElements` (and its inner `isHidden`) keep #116's names but now also drop locked elements. Renaming would mean editing #116's tests.
- `excalidraw-app/tests/collabLock.test.tsx` duplicates ~60 lines of socket/encryption/Firebase mocks from `collabVisibility.test.tsx` (`vi.mock` is per file).
- The dropdown trigger's badge still only reflects _hidden_ collaborators, not locked ones: including locks would change #116's badge behavior, since Criteria C keeps collaborators locked after they're shown again.
- Known limitations: a locked collaborator's arrow bound to _my_ shape still follows it when I move my shape (binding is kept, as in #116); hyperlinks on locked elements can't be clicked (locked elements behave like empty canvas for hit testing).

**Encountered:**

- `getLocallyVisibleElements` serves both export and the bindable-element list in `App.tsx`, mixing "visible" with "interactive". Harmless for this PR (binding is visibility-only by design).
- `packages/element/tests/frame.test.tsx` has 30 skipped tests from upstream commit `0f81c302` (#7194, 2023); unrelated, untouched.
- In jsdom the viewport is 0×0, so the eraser (which only considers on-screen elements) can only be tested on shapes at the origin.
- The repo's `yarn prettier <files>` script already includes `.`, so it formats the whole repo rather than the given files.
- Locally, `yarn test:code` crashes when `excalidraw-room/node_modules` is installed (two copies of `@typescript-eslint`); see Test Evidence.

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

- **A real two-browser session over the network.** The collab tests drive the real `Collab`/`Portal` classes, but the socket, encryption, and Firebase are mocked. Verified manually in two browsers with the local `excalidraw-room` server (all ACs checked by the author).
- **Visual appearance** (lock icon states, disabled styling, tooltips, dark mode, row layout). jsdom doesn't render CSS; verified manually.

# File 1: `packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorLock.test.tsx` (90 tests)

**Shared setup:** a real Excalidraw editor in a fake room with four buckets:

- **me**: the current user
- **alice**: in the room
- **carol**: previously seen (in the directory, no longer live)
- **miscellaneous**: an untagged element, plus "dave", a creator this client has never seen

`OTHERS` = alice, carol and miscellaneous (everyone I'm allowed to lock).

Helpers: `execute(name)` runs an action by name; `getRow(id)` reads a dropdown row's data (`isHidden`, `isLocked`, `isLockDisabled`); `lockedIds()` reads `lockedCollaboratorIds`.

## Criteria A: per-collaborator toggle

**AC-A: nobody is locked by default** Checks that the lock list starts empty and no row shows locked. A says locking is something _I_ do, so a fresh session must start fully interactive.

**AC-A: toggling a collaborator's lock locks them, toggling again unlocks them** Runs the toggle on alice twice: first the list is `["alice"]` and her row shows locked, then it's empty again. This is A's "locking… / unlocking makes them interactive again", in both directions.

**AC-A: locking leaves the collaborator visible** After locking alice, nobody is hidden and her row isn't hidden. A says locked means _visible_ but non-interactive, so a lock must never hide anyone.

**AC-A: locking one collaborator doesn't lock anyone else** Locks carol only, and checks that alice and miscellaneous stay unlocked. A says the toggle is _per collaborator_, so it mustn't leak to other rows.

**AC-A: a visible collaborator's lock toggle is enabled** Alice's and carol's toggles aren't disabled. A requires a usable toggle; C only disables it for _hidden_ collaborators.

## Miscellaneous bucket

**AC-A (misc): the miscellaneous bucket can be locked and unlocked like any collaborator** Toggles the miscellaneous bucket on, then off. A explicitly says the toggle includes the "unknown / miscellaneous" bucket.

**AC-A (misc): the miscellaneous row's lock toggle is enabled while visible** Same as above, but for the toggle's enabled state.

**AC-B (misc): Lock all includes the miscellaneous bucket** After Lock all, the lock list contains the miscellaneous bucket. B says "every listed collaborator", and the miscellaneous row is listed.

**AC-C (misc): hiding the miscellaneous bucket shows it locked and disables its toggle** C applies to every row, the miscellaneous one included.

## Criteria B: bulk controls

**AC-B: Lock all locks every listed collaborator (except me, see AC-H)** After Lock all, the list is exactly `OTHERS`. That's every listed row minus me, because H says I'm never in the lock list.

**AC-B: Lock all doesn't hide anyone** Locking is visible-only, so the bulk version mustn't hide anyone either.

**AC-B: Unlock all unlocks every visible collaborator** Lock all, then Unlock all, leaves the list empty, because everyone was visible.

**AC-B: Unlock all leaves hidden collaborators non-interactive** Locks alice, hides carol, then runs Unlock all. Alice is unlocked; carol still shows locked and her toggle is disabled. This is B's exact wording: "hidden collaborators stay non-interactive."

**AC-B + AC-C: a collaborator hidden during Unlock all is still locked once shown again** Hides carol, runs Unlock all, then shows carol: she's visible but still locked. Combining B with C's "stay locked until I unlock them" means Unlock all mustn't quietly unlock hidden people for later.

## Criteria C: no interactivity without visibility

**AC-C: a hidden collaborator's lock toggle shows locked and is disabled** Hiding alice makes her row locked and disabled. C: "lock toggle shows as locked and can't be changed."

**AC-C: a hidden collaborator can't be unlocked** Locks alice, hides her, tries to toggle her lock, then shows her: she's still locked. The toggle attempt while she was hidden was ignored, as "can't be changed" requires.

**AC-C: toggling the lock of a hidden, never-locked collaborator changes nothing** Hides alice, who was never locked, tries to toggle, then shows her: still locked. Hiding her locked her (C), and the toggle attempt mustn't have flipped that.

**AC-C: shown again individually, a collaborator stays locked until I unlock them** Hides and then shows alice. She's locked, her toggle is now enabled, and one click unlocks her. This is C's second sentence, word for word.

**AC-C: after Hide all → Show all, everyone stays locked until I unlock them (except me, see AC-H)** This is the rule you confirmed when we kept C as written: the bulk show also leaves people locked. The lock list equals `OTHERS`.

**AC-C: showing a collaborator who was locked before hiding keeps them locked** Locks carol, hides her, shows her: still locked. Hiding and showing must never _remove_ a lock.

## Criteria G: local and non-persistent

**AC-G: lock settings are not saved to local storage** `clearAppStateForLocalStorage` (what the app actually saves) has no `lockedCollaboratorIds`. G says "resets when the page reloads", so the setting must never be written to storage.

**AC-G: lock settings are not included in exports** Same check on `cleanAppStateForExport`. A saved file must not carry my local locks.

**AC-G: lock settings are not sent to the server / other collaborators** Same check on `clearAppStateForDatabase`. G says "apply only to my client."

**AC-G: lock settings reset when the page reloads** Simulates a reload: it takes what would be saved and restores it with `restoreAppState`. The lock list comes back empty, matching G's "reset when the page reloads, matching #116."

## Criteria H: my own drawings

**AC-H: I can't lock myself** Toggling "me" leaves the list empty and my row unlocked. H: "not in the lock list."

**AC-H: my own row's lock toggle is disabled and shows unlocked** This is how we agreed H should look in the UI.

**AC-H: Lock all never puts me in the lock list** **AC-H: Hide all → Show all never puts me in the lock list** Both bulk paths that add people must skip me. Hide all _hides_ me (#116's view-mode behaviour), but must not lock me.

**AC-H: a lock list set from outside never makes my row locked** A host app writes `me` straight into the lock list, and my row still shows unlocked. H says "always stay interactive", so the rule itself, not just the buttons, must ignore me.

## Bulk button availability (`getBulkLockAvailability`)

These test the pure function behind the fix for your manual-testing bug, using hand-built rows (my row is always disabled).

**AC-B: with a visible, unlocked collaborator only Lock all applies** Lock all would change something and Unlock all wouldn't.

**AC-B: with every visible collaborator locked only Unlock all applies** The reverse case.

**AC-B: with visible locked and unlocked collaborators both apply** In a mixed state, both buttons have work to do.

**AC-C: hidden collaborators (locked, can't change) count for neither** This is your bug in its purest form: when everyone is hidden, both buttons are disabled.

**AC-H: my own row counts for neither** Having just my row, which can never change, doesn't enable anything.

**AC-B: previously seen collaborators count too** B says "every listed collaborator", and previously seen people are listed.

## Enforcement setup

Two solid 100×100 squares: **my rectangle at x 0–100**, **alice's at x 200–300**. The solid fill means a click inside counts as a hit. `lockAlice()` runs her toggle. Interactions use real pointer and keyboard events through the editor.

**(control) clicking an unlocked collaborator's element selects it** Proves the click lands on alice's square. Without this, the next test could pass simply because the click missed.

**AC-D: clicking a locked element selects nothing (like empty canvas)** The same click after locking selects nothing. D: "behaves like clicking empty canvas."

**AC-D: clicking a locked element selects the unlocked element underneath it** Carol's square sits exactly under alice's locked one; the click selects carol's. D: "…or selects an unlocked element underneath it."

**(control) a marquee over both selects both** **AC-D: a marquee over locked and unlocked elements selects only the unlocked ones** The same drag box covers both squares: both get selected when unlocked, only mine after locking. D's mixed-marquee sentence, verbatim.

**AC-D: Select All (Ctrl/Cmd+A) skips locked elements** Ctrl+A selects only mine. D names Select All explicitly.

**AC-D: locking a collaborator deselects their selected elements** Selects both, then locks alice: only mine stays selected. Without this, an element selected _before_ locking could still be moved or deleted, which would break E through the back door.

**AC-D: a locked element can't be selected even when the selection is set directly** Forces alice's square into the selection through the API, and the safety net removes it. D says "never selected", whatever code path tries.

**AC-D: selecting my member of a mixed group never selects the locked member** My square and alice's share a group. Clicking mine selects only mine, not the group. Normally clicking a group member selects the whole group, which would reach her element.

## Criteria E: changes

**AC-E: dragging a locked element doesn't move it** **(control) dragging an unlocked element moves it** The same drag on alice's square: her position is unchanged when locked, and changes when unlocked.

The control proves the stroke erases; the locked test proves locking blocks it; the third test proves locking doesn't break the eraser for my own shapes.

**(control) double-clicking an unlocked text element edits it** **AC-E: double-clicking a locked text element doesn't edit it** E: "can't be… text-edited by double-click."

**(control) double-clicking an unlocked shape adds a label to it** **AC-E: double-clicking a locked shape doesn't add a label to it** Adding a label changes the shape and can resize it. When locked, the new text isn't attached and her shape's bound elements are unchanged.

**AC-E (amended): a new arrow can still bind to a locked element** My arrow drawn onto alice's locked square attaches to it. This is your amendment to E.

**AC-E (amended): binding to a locked element doesn't move, resize, or rotate it** Your condition was "shouldn't force objects to move or snap", so her square's position, size and angle are unchanged.

**AC-C: a new arrow can't bind to a hidden (and so non-interactive) element** Hidden still blocks binding: "if not visible, can't bind."

## Criteria C: enforcement

**AC-C: a hidden collaborator is non-interactive even if they're not in the lock list** Sets "hidden" without "locked" directly, and Ctrl+A still selects only mine. This proves the rule itself enforces "no interactivity without visibility", not just the bookkeeping that keeps the two lists in step.

**AC-C: shown again after hiding, a collaborator's elements still can't be selected** Hide, then show alice, then click her square: nothing is selected. C's "stay locked" on the canvas, not just in the dropdown.

**AC-H: my own elements stay selectable even if my id is put on the lock list** My id is forced into the list, and clicking my square still selects it.

**AC-H: Lock all leaves my own elements interactive** After Lock all, Ctrl+A still selects my square.

## Criteria F: editor side

**AC-F: locking and unlocking change no element versions** Records every element's `version` and `versionNonce`, then runs four lock actions: all unchanged. Any version change would get synced, and F says "element versions stay the same."

# File 2: `packages/element/src/__tests__/ownershipLock.test.ts` (40 tests)

These are pure unit tests: no editor, just the functions in `ownership.ts`. StrykerJS will mutate this file most, so each `if`, `!` and `?.` has a test that would catch it being flipped.

## `isCollaboratorInteractive`: the one rule

**AC-A: a bucket that is neither hidden nor locked is interactive** → true **AC-A: a locked, visible bucket is not interactive** → false **AC-C: a hidden bucket is not interactive even if it isn't locked** → false. This is your principle, that interactivity never exists without visibility. **AC-C: a hidden and locked bucket is not interactive** → false **AC-A: locking one bucket doesn't affect another** → bob is interactive when only alice is locked. **AC-H: my own bucket stays interactive even if it is in the lock list** → true, because the self check runs before the lock check. **AC-C over AC-H: my own hidden bucket is not interactive** → false. Hidden is checked _first_, so even I lose interactivity when hidden, which matches #116's view-mode behaviour. **AC-A (misc): the miscellaneous bucket can be locked** → false **AC-G: with no lock or visibility state (e.g. outside a room) everything is interactive** → true. Missing sets must default to "interactive", never crash or block. **without a known self id, a locked bucket is still not interactive** → false. If my id is unknown (`null`), the self exemption mustn't accidentally unlock anyone.

## `addLockedCollaborators` (used by Lock all and by hiding)

**AC-B: adds every given bucket to the lock list** **AC-B: keeps buckets that were already locked.** It adds; it never replaces. **AC-H: never adds me** **AC-G: doesn't mutate the current lock list.** React state must be replaced, not edited in place, or the editor won't notice the change. **accepts a missing lock list.** Handles a lock list that doesn't exist yet.

## `toggleLockedCollaborator` (the per-row button)

**AC-A: locks an unlocked, visible bucket** **AC-A: unlocks a locked, visible bucket** **AC-A: leaves other buckets' locks unchanged** **AC-C: can't unlock a hidden bucket** **AC-C: can't change the lock of a hidden bucket that isn't in the list.** Ignored in both directions while hidden. **AC-H: can't lock me** **AC-G: doesn't mutate the current lock list**

## `unlockVisibleCollaborators` (Unlock all)

**AC-B: unlocks every visible bucket** → empty list **AC-B + AC-C: hidden buckets stay locked, so they're still locked once shown** → `["bob"]` **AC-C: a hidden bucket that wasn't in the lock list ends up locked.** If someone was hidden by the host app without being locked, Unlock all fixes that, so C still holds after they're shown again. **AC-H: never locks me, even when I'm hidden**

## `getSelfCreatorId` (finds "me")

**AC-H: returns the current user's client id** **returns null without a current user** **returns null when the current user has no client id yet.** This happens briefly while joining a room. **returns null outside of a room (no collaborators)** H depends on knowing who "me" is, so each way of _not_ knowing must fail safely.

## `isElementInteractive` (the rule applied to an element)

**AC-D: an element of a locked collaborator is not interactive** **(control) an element of an unlocked collaborator is interactive** **AC-H: my own element stays interactive even if I'm in the lock list** **AC-A (misc): an untagged element follows the miscellaneous bucket's lock** **AC-A (misc): a never-seen creator's element follows the miscellaneous bucket's lock.** "dave" isn't in the directory, so his elements count as miscellaneous, matching #116's rule. **AC-D: a label follows its container's lock, not its own creator's.** My label on alice's locked shape is locked too; otherwise you could edit text inside her shape.

## `excludeNonInteractiveElements` (the filter version)

**returns the same array when nobody is hidden or locked.** A performance shortcut for the hit-test hot path; the same array means no copying. **AC-D: drops locked collaborators' elements** **AC-C: drops hidden collaborators' elements** **AC-H: keeps my own elements even if I'm in the lock list**

# File 3: `excalidraw-app/tests/collabLock.test.tsx` (4 tests)

This file runs the **real** collaboration classes (`Collab` and `Portal`). The socket is a fake that records every message the client would send; encryption is a passthrough. A peer's element ("theirs", by alice) is delivered first, the way it would arrive from the room.

**(control) a local edit is sent to the room** Adds an element of mine, then waits for an update containing it. This proves the recording socket really captures sends. Sending is asynchronous, which is why the original version of this test failed.

**AC-F: locking and unlocking sends nothing new to other collaborators** Runs all four lock actions and syncs, then makes one "marker" edit. Messages go out in order, so if the first update after locking is the marker, locking itself sent nothing. Checking a message count straight away could pass falsely, before the async send finished. F: "sends nothing new to other collaborators."

**AC-F: locking and unlocking change no element versions** The same version check as the editor-level test, but with real sync running. Versions are what decide whether anything gets broadcast.

**AC-F: a peer's edit to a locked collaborator's element still arrives** Locks everyone, then a peer moves "theirs" to x=500, and my client shows the move. F: "Other collaborators can still… edit… as before." The lock filters only _my_ interactions, never incoming changes.

Yes. Re-checking the code against your rule ("their functionality should not force objects to move or snap") turned up a few gaps I haven't raised with you. The first one is a real hole in Criteria E.

## 1. Locked elements can still be moved indirectly (needs your decision)

The direct paths are blocked, since you can't select a locked element. Two _indirect_ paths still move one when I move **my own** element:

- **Frames:** dragging my frame also drags everything inside it ([dragElements.ts:81-87](packages/element/src/dragElements.ts#L81-L87)). If Bob's locked shapes sit in my frame, they move, and the move syncs to everyone.
- **Path snapping:** dragging a path also drags the elements it targets, and dragging an element drags any path targeting it ([dragElements.ts:93-102](packages/element/src/dragElements.ts#L93-L102)). If Bob's locked shape is my path's target, or Bob's locked path targets my shape, his element moves.

Neither path is tested. #116 has the same gap for _hidden_ elements, so a hidden shape inside my frame moves too, unseen.

**Options:**

- **(a) Block it:** skip locked or hidden elements when gathering what a drag moves. This matches E's text and your rule. Side effect: a locked shape can end up outside my frame's new position while still belonging to it, so it gets clipped on screen.
- **(b) Allow it:** document it as a known limitation, like the bound arrow that follows my shape.
- **(c) Refuse the drag:** don't let me drag a frame or path that has locked elements attached.

**My recommendation is (a)**, with tests. It's the only option that keeps E literally true, and the fix is small: one filter in `dragElements.ts` using the same rule function.

## 2. Deleting my frame edits locked children (smaller, needs your decision)

Deleting a frame doesn't delete its children: it detaches them by setting `frameId: null` ([actionDeleteSelected.tsx:117-122](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionDeleteSelected.tsx#L117-L122)). For Bob's locked shapes that's a synced edit, though nothing moves or disappears. I'd **accept and document** this, the same as arrow binding. Leaving them attached to a deleted frame risks broken data.

## 3. Untested, but I believe safe

- **Lasso selection and the path-target pick:** both go through the rule, but neither has a dedicated test. The PR already lists them.
- **Search:** locked text still shows up in search results, which is correct since it's visible. If jumping to a result ever selected the element, the safety net would deselect it. Not tested.
- **A text editor already open when someone gets locked:** unreachable from the UI, because opening the dropdown closes the editor first. A host app setting the lock directly could leave it open. Not tested.

## 4. Already mentioned, but easy to miss

- The issue's **Summary** still says "bind to", which contradicts amended E.
- I re-ran the **full suite** before the encoding repair, not after. The repair only changed test names, and that file passes 90/90, but you may want one final full run before submitting.
- **StrykerJS on `App.tsx`:** it's about 13k lines, so it'll be slow. All of the lock logic lives in `ownership.ts` and `visibility.ts`; App.tsx only has one-line calls.
- **Undoing edits made before locking** (Ctrl+Z after locking can still revert a change you made to Bob's element earlier) is **out of scope** per the issue, but a reviewer may well ask about it.

How do you want to handle items 1 and 2? If you choose (a) for item 1, I'll write the tests first (a frame drag and a path drag with a locked element, each with a control), add the filter, run everything again, commit, and update `pr-81.md`.

# Issue #81: final summary

## 1. The idea in one rule

Each collaborator, including "Untagged & unknown", has two local settings on your client: **hidden** (from #116) and **locked** (new). One pure function decides whether you can interact with their drawings:

```
isCollaboratorInteractive(bucket):
  hidden?       → NO   (no interactivity without visibility, AC-C)
  is it me?     → YES  (my drawings can't be locked, AC-H)
  locked?       → NO   (visible but non-interactive, AC-A)
  otherwise     → YES
```

Visibility (rendering, export, search, **arrow binding**) still uses #116's "is it hidden?" check. Interaction (selecting, editing, erasing) uses this rule, so a locked element is visible but untouchable, and a hidden one is neither.

## 2. Flow: clicking the lock button

```
Dropdown row 🔓 click
  └─ actionToggleCollaboratorLock(bucket)
       └─ toggleLockedCollaborator()        ← pure: ignored if hidden or me
            └─ appState.lockedCollaboratorIds = new Set(...)
                 (captureUpdate NEVER → no undo entry, nothing synced)
  └─ App.componentDidUpdate sees the lock list changed
       └─ selection safety net drops any now-locked selected elements
  └─ dropdown re-renders: rows read isLocked / isLockDisabled,
     bulk buttons read getBulkLockAvailability()
```

Hiding someone (their eye toggle, or Hide all) also adds them to the lock list, so they're still locked after being shown again (C). Unlock all keeps hidden people locked (B).

## 3. Flow: trying to interact with a locked element

```
pointer / keyboard / eraser event
  ├─ click, double-click edit, path pick → hit test (App.getElementsAtPosition,
  │      getTextBindableContainerAtPosition)  → locked elements = empty canvas
  ├─ marquee, lasso, Ctrl+A, groups       → selectGroupsForSelectedElements
  │      (groups.ts)                          → locked elements filtered out
  ├─ selection set any other way          → App safety net → removed
  ├─ move / resize / rotate / delete      → act on the selection → nothing to act on
  └─ eraser                               → candidates filtered by the rule
                     all of them call ──►  isElementInteractive  ──►  the rule
```

**Kept on purpose** (your decisions):

- Arrows can bind to locked elements; hidden ones still can't be bound to.
- Dragging my frame moves locked elements inside it.
- Bound arrows follow my shapes, and path targets follow my path.
- Deleting my frame leaves locked children where they are.

## 4. What changed, file by file

| Area | File | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rule | [ownership.ts](packages/element/src/ownership.ts) | `isCollaboratorInteractive`; lock-list helpers (`addLockedCollaborators`, `toggleLockedCollaborator`, `unlockVisibleCollaborators`); `getSelfCreatorId`; element-level `isElementInteractive` and `excludeNonInteractiveElements` |
| State | [types.ts](packages/excalidraw/types.ts), [appState.ts](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts) | `lockedCollaboratorIds`: empty by default; never saved, exported or synced (G) |
| Actions | [actionCollaboratorVisibility.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCollaboratorVisibility.ts), [actions/index.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/index.ts), [actions/types.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/types.ts) | Toggle lock, Lock all, Unlock all; #116's hide actions also lock whoever they hide |
| Enforcement | [groups.ts](packages/element/src/groups.ts) | Selection filter for marquee, lasso, Select All and groups |
|  | [App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx) | Hit tests, path pick, and the safety net (now also re-runs on lock changes) |
|  | [eraser/index.ts](packages/excalidraw/eraser/index.ts) | Eraser candidates and group members |
|  | [visibility.ts](packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts) | `isElementInteractiveLocally`; safety net uses the rule; row fields `isLocked` / `isLockDisabled`; `getBulkLockAvailability` |
| UI | [CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/CollaboratorVisibility/CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx), [.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/CollaboratorVisibility/CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.scss), [en.json](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json) | Lock button beside each eye; Lock all / Unlock all, disabled when they'd change nothing; same on desktop and phone |
| Snapshots | 4 `.snap` files | Only add the `"lockedCollaboratorIds": Set {}` key |

**Not changed:** arrow binding (`binding.ts`, `focus.ts`, `getBindableElements`), frame-under-cursor, the renderer, export and search, where the dropdown is mounted (`LayerUI`, `MainMenu`), and every #116 test.

| [collabLock.test.tsx](excalidraw-app/tests/collabLock.test.tsx) (4) | App and collab integration (real `Collab`/`Portal`, socket that records sends) | **F**: nothing sent on lock or unlock (proved with a marker message), versions unchanged, peers' edits to locked elements still arrive, plus a control |
